description: Counts of how American friends take turns when they talk: turn length, short-turn share, question rate, reaction tokens, turn openers and hedges. Counts and one- to three-word tokens only; no line from the corpus ships.

source.document: Santa Barbara Corpus of Spoken American English, Parts 1 to 4
source.publisher: University of California, Santa Barbara, Department of Linguistics

coverage: The 10 recordings the corpus describes as friends, roommates or neighbors talking: an after-dinner conversation, friends cooking dinner, three retired women before lunch, friends visiting, two male friends, a block party, friends in a living room, four roommates and a dinner party. Recordings 2, 3, 11, 15, 17, 32, 44, 45, 50 and 51.

mining.turnRule: A turn is the run of transcript lines by one speaker until another speaker begins.
mining.selection: Chosen from each recording's own description on the corpus page; family, work, classroom and public talk are left out.
